Definition: from G575 and G4105; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth):--err, seduce.
BiblicalUsage: Two uses, and in both someone is led astray. The love of money is the root of all evil, and some coveting after it have erred from the faith in 1 Timothy 6:10; and false Christs and false prophets shall rise and show signs and wonders to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect in Mark 13:22.
TheologicalSignificance: The word is a wandering off the road — and Paul and Jesus agree on where the road bends: money and miracles.
